summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR113 crores and EBITDA 28% to INR23 crores (~20% margin), with PAT near INR8 crores held back by H2 hiring.
summary.overview: Emmforce reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about INR113 crores, up 27% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR23 crores (up 28%) and PAT of about INR8 crores. Management attributed the PAT moderation to manpower hired ahead of the US export programme and higher depreciation from EMSPL and capacity capex. The US OEM export order contributed only about INR5.5-6 crores, all in March 2026, after production started in December 2025 and final customer go-ahead came end-February. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR195 crores (INR165 crores automotive plus INR30 crores agri) and FY28 of about INR240 crores, with EBITDA margins of 20-22% and PAT near 10%.

segments.name: Automotive (drivetrain, US OEM and aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity about INR200 crores with utilisation of 50-55%. FY26 automotive revenue about INR105 crores; FY27 target INR165 crores, with the ~INR60 crores increment mainly from the US export order. About 40% of automotive revenue expected from OEMs by end-FY27; management sees OEM share reaching ~60% over time.

segments.name: Agri (rotavator blades, parts, EMSPL)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity about INR150 crores with utilisation of 8-10%. Revenue run-rate about INR4 crores per half in FY26 (commercial sales from July 2025 per analyst question, TAFE sales from January 2026); FY27 target INR30 crores and FY28 target about INR50 crores. TAFE initially ordering about INR15 lakh per month, with its total monthly requirement of about INR35-50 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target about INR195 crores: INR165 crores automotive and INR30 crores agri; management said the INR190-195 crore figure is tracking in line for the current two months.
FY28 revenue target about INR240 crores, with agri contributing about INR50 crores.
EBITDA margin target 20-22% and PAT margin around 10% for coming years.
Order book exceeds INR500 crores, but management said only about INR60 crores per annum is executable, spread over the next eight years.
Asset turnover (gross basis) about 3x in FY26, rising to 3.5-4x in FY27.
Working capital to be funded from sanctioned bank lines and US export credit of up to six months; management said equity dilution is not needed and is open to invoice factoring.
No new product category planned for at least the next year; hydraulic gear pumps to become a separate division, though no numbers disclosed yet.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about INR350 crores (automotive ~INR200 crores, agri ~INR150 crores) against FY26 revenue of INR113 crores.
Dedicated greenfield US OEM facility commissioned; mass production started 15 December 2025.

EMSPL (agri and forging subsidiary) completed first year; houses a 1,600-tonne forging press and a fully automated rotavator blade line with major equipment from Japan; turned from cash loss to modest cash profit.
Facilities total about 150,000 sq ft in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, with 600+ staff; R&D spend about 2% of revenue.
Capex in FY26 executed ahead of revenue ramp (capacity, backward integration, automation, forging, infrastructure) across automotive and agri.
demand_pricing: Management said the US customer visit (about two weeks, roughly 10 days before the call) showed positive response; orders above expectations and no recession signs seen.
Management said there is no dampness in demand so far; OEM business running at over INR5 crores per month and aftermarket doing well.

FY26 H2 revenue flat versus H1 on the base business; management attributed this to US customers running down inventory after the 25% tariff, with inventory rationalisation still ongoing while new orders came in.
Freight cost rose only slightly despite West Asia conflict; shipments on time; dollar realisations better per management.
TAFE blade order: initial share of about INR15 lakh per month, potential to reach 70-80% of its INR35-50 lakh monthly requirement.

New business of INR10-12 crores with PPAP samples submitted, commercial production expected Q3 FY27; another US bid order close to INR10 crores annually; long-term drivetrain order worth about INR10.5 crores per year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the final FY26 revenue from the large export order, and does it explain the margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.5-6 crores, all in March 2026. Management said the H2 employee cost increase (~INR6 crores to ~INR8 crores) was 90-100% due to this order's hires, with some senior hires for future expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Why is base business flat in H2 and what is the outlook excluding the export order?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers reduced inventory after 25% US tariffs hit their cash flows. Management said orders have since picked up more than expected and there is no visible slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: What gives visibility to scale agri from about INR4 crores per half to INR30 crores in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited full-season sales through Diwali, TAFE approvals and consistent ordering, distributor orders in Maharashtra, Karnataka and MP, and talks with large OEMs on blades and contract manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR500 crore order book is executable in FY27-28, and why is FY27 base growth absent from guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crores per annum, spread over eight years. Management said guidance was kept conservative; the INR60 crore export increment is the only increase in the automotive FY27 figure over FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is working capital funding need and will equity be diluted?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank working capital is already sanctioned; US export transit is about two months and credit up to six months. Management said no equity dilution is needed and it is looking at factoring.

qa_highlights.question: Is there margin pressure from OEM business or input-cost headwinds (crude, war)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets niche parts with no pricing pressure, sees no margin dampness, and freight increase has been minor. Margin drag was attributed to manpower cost for the new project.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the group company merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entity is a group company, not a subsidiary, and merger work is ongoing with a possible announcement in the coming months.

risks_watch: FY27 guidance requires automotive to rise from ~INR105 crores to ~INR165 crores; the ~INR60 crore increment depends mainly on one US export order, with its run-rate ramp still early.
Agri target of INR30 crores (vs ~INR8 crores in FY26) rests on TAFE scaling and on OEM talks that management would not detail; seasonality limits sales to about Diwali.
Working capital is elevated and rising with US export receivables; funding relies on bank lines and possible factoring.
Utilisation is only 50-55% in automotive and 8-10% in agri; margin recovery depends on hitting volumes.
Customer inventory rationalisation is still ongoing per management; watch H1 FY27 order flow.
Pending merger of the group company; no timeline or terms given. Hydraulic pump division has no disclosed numbers yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and FY27-28 visibility, but evasive on specifics: it declined to detail the OEM pipeline or agri talks, and gave no base-business growth driver beyond the US order. Answers on margin and risk were generic, and the call had audio issues that interrupted several questions.
